    IsIso (whiskerRight α F) :=
  (isoWhiskerRight (asIso α) F).isIso_hom

@[simp, to_dual self]
theorem inv_whiskerRight {G H : C ⥤ D} (α : G ⟶ H) (F : D ⥤ E) [IsIso α] :
    inv (whiskerRight α F) = whiskerRight (inv α) F := by
  symm
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_inv_hom_id
  simp [← whiskerRight_comp]

@[simp, to_dual self]
theorem inv_whiskerLeft (F : C ⥤ D) {G H : D ⥤ E} (α : G ⟶ H) [IsIso α] :
    inv (whiskerLeft F α) = whiskerLeft F (inv α) := by
  symm
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_inv_hom_id
  simp [← whiskerLeft_comp]

@[simp, reassoc]
theorem isoWhiskerLeft_trans (F : C ⥤ D) {G H K : D ⥤ E} (α : G ≅ H) (β : H ≅ K) :

/-- Composition of two isomorphisms -/
@[simps (attr := grind =)]
def trans (α : X ≅ Y) (β : Y ≅ Z) : X ≅ Z where
  hom := α.hom ≫ β.hom
  inv := β.inv ≫ α.inv

instance instTransIso : Trans (α := C) (· ≅ ·) (· ≅ ·) (· ≅ ·) where

infixr:80 " ≪≫ " => Iso.trans -- type as `\ll \gg`.

-- Annotating this with `@[grind =]` triggers a run-away chain of `Category.assoc` instantiations.
-- Hopefully this can be restored when `grind` has support for associative/commutative operations,
-- or direct support for category theory.
@[simp, to_dual self]
theorem trans_mk {X Y Z : C} (hom : X ⟶ Y) (inv : Y ⟶ X) (hom_inv_id) (inv_hom_id)
    (hom' : Y ⟶ Z) (inv' : Z ⟶ Y) (hom_inv_id') (inv_hom_id') (hom_inv_id'') (inv_hom_id'') :
    Iso.trans ⟨hom, inv, hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id⟩ ⟨hom', inv', hom_inv_id', inv_hom_id'⟩ =
     ⟨hom ≫ hom', inv' ≫ inv, hom_inv_id'', inv_hom_id''⟩ :=
  rfl

@[simp, grind _=_]
theorem trans_symm (α : X ≅ Y) (β : Y ≅ Z) : (α ≪≫ β).symm = β.symm ≪≫ α.symm :=
  rfl

@[simp, grind _=_]
theorem trans_assoc {Z' : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (β : Y ≅ Z) (γ : Z ≅ Z') :
    (α ≪≫ β) ≪≫ γ = α ≪≫ β ≪≫ γ := by
  ext; simp only [trans_hom, Category.assoc]

@[simp]
theorem refl_trans (α : X ≅ Y) : Iso.refl X ≪≫ α = α := by ext; apply Category.id_comp

@[simp]
theorem trans_refl (α : X ≅ Y) : α ≪≫ Iso.refl Y = α := by ext; apply Category.comp_id

@[simp]
theorem symm_self_id (α : X ≅ Y) : α.symm ≪≫ α = Iso.refl Y :=
  ext α.inv_hom_id

@[simp]
theorem self_symm_id (α : X ≅ Y) : α ≪≫ α.symm = Iso.refl X :=
  ext α.hom_inv_id

@[simp]
theorem symm_self_id_assoc (α : X ≅ Y) (β : Y ≅ Z) : α.symm ≪≫ α ≪≫ β = β := by
  rw [← trans_assoc, symm_self_id, refl_trans]

@[simp]
theorem self_symm_id_assoc (α : X ≅ Y) (β : X ≅ Z) : α ≪≫ α.symm ≪≫ β = β := by
  rw [← trans_assoc, self_symm_id, refl_trans]

@[to_dual none]
theorem inv_comp_eq (α : X ≅ Y) {f : X ⟶ Z} {g : Y ⟶ Z} : α.inv ≫ f = g ↔ f = α.hom ≫ g :=
  ⟨fun H => by simp [H.symm], fun H => by simp [H]⟩

I’m factoring that square into a local transport lemma; its component proof will contain no Picard data and no naturality argument.

@[simp]
theorem isoWhiskerLeft_hom (F : C ⥤ D) {G H : D ⥤ E} (α : G ≅ H) :
    (isoWhiskerLeft F α).hom = whiskerLeft F α.hom :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem isoWhiskerLeft_inv (F : C ⥤ D) {G H : D ⥤ E} (α : G ≅ H) :
    (isoWhiskerLeft F α).inv = whiskerLeft F α.inv :=
  rfl

lemma isoWhiskerLeft_symm (F : C ⥤ D) {G H : D ⥤ E} (α : G ≅ H) :
    (isoWhiskerLeft F α).symm = isoWhiskerLeft F α.symm :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma isoWhiskerLeft_refl (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) :
    isoWhiskerLeft F (Iso.refl G) = Iso.refl _ :=
  rfl

/-- If `α : G ≅ H` then
`isoWhiskerRight α F : (G ⋙ F) ≅ (H ⋙ F)` has components `F.map_iso (α.app X)`.
-/
def isoWhiskerRight {G H : C ⥤ D} (α : G ≅ H) (F : D ⥤ E) : G ⋙ F ≅ H ⋙ F :=
  ((whiskeringRight C D E).obj F).mapIso α

@[simp]
theorem isoWhiskerRight_hom {G H : C ⥤ D} (α : G ≅ H) (F : D ⥤ E) :
    (isoWhiskerRight α F).hom = whiskerRight α.hom F :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem isoWhiskerRight_inv {G H : C ⥤ D} (α : G ≅ H) (F : D ⥤ E) :
    (isoWhiskerRight α F).inv = whiskerRight α.inv F :=
  rfl

lemma isoWhiskerRight_symm {G H : C ⥤ D} (α : G ≅ H) (F : D ⥤ E) :
    (isoWhiskerRight α F).symm = isoWhiskerRight α.symm F :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma isoWhiskerRight_refl (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) :
    isoWhiskerRight (Iso.refl F) G = Iso.refl _ := by
  cat_disch

     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RepresentableByCocycle
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RepresentableByTransport
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# The tensor-overlap comparison for Picard representability
    13	
    14	For a field extension `k → L`, the two coprojections
    15	`L → L ⊗[k] L` induce two pullbacks of an L-side representation.  This file
    16	constructs the comparison between those two representing schemes.  Each pullback
    17	is obtained from `Over.mapPullbackAdj`; the presheaf comparison is assembled from
    18	the landed theta isomorphism and the equality of the two composites back to `k`.
    19	
    20	Over the triple tensor product, the three actual Amitsur faces determine three maps
    21	back to `Spec L`.  The corresponding Picard comparisons are defined independently
    22	through a common k-side functor, and Yoneda uniqueness turns their natural-isomorphism
    23	cocycle into the representing-scheme cocycle.  In particular, the `1,3` comparison is
    24	not defined as the composite of the other two.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	set_option autoImplicit false
    28	
    29	universe u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory
    32	open scoped TensorProduct
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	variable {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    37	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	
    41	/-! ## The two tensor coprojections and their common base map -/
    42	
    43	/-- The first map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
    44	noncomputable def tensorOverlapInl :
    45	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
    46	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    47	    (tensorInl (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    48	
    49	/-- The second map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
    50	noncomputable def tensorOverlapInr :
    51	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
    52	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    53	    (tensorInr (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    54	
    55	/-- The common map to `Spec k` obtained from either tensor coprojection. -/
    56	noncomputable def tensorOverlapBase :
    57	    Spec (.of L) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
    58	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))
    59	
    60	/-- The two tensor coprojections have the same composite to the challenge base. -/
    61	lemma tensorOverlapInl_comp_base :
    62	    tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L) =
    63	      tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L) := by
    64	  simp only [tensorOverlapInl, tensorOverlapInr, tensorOverlapBase]
    65	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
    66	  have h := tensorInl_comp_ofId (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)
    67	  congr 1
    68	  ext x
    69	  exact DFunLike.congr_fun h x
    70	
    71	/-! ## The presheaf comparison -/
    72	
    73	/-- Rebase the L-side Picard functor along an arbitrary map to `Spec L`, then identify
    74	it with the k-side functor over the composite base map. -/
    75	noncomputable def pic0BaseCommon {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : S ⟶ Spec (.of L)) :
    76	    (Over.map f).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
    77	      (Over.map (f ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    78	        pic0TypeFunctor C :=
    79	  Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafCommon
    80	    (tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L)) (pic0ThetaType k L C) f
    81	
    82	/-- Rebase an L-side Picard functor along one tensor coprojection, then identify it
    83	with the fixed k-side functor through theta and the common composite to `Spec k`. -/
    84	noncomputable def tensorOverlapCommon
    85	    (f : Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L)) :
    86	    (Over.map f).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
    87	      (Over.map (f ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    88	        pic0TypeFunctor C :=
    89	  pic0BaseCommon (C := C) f
    90	
    91	/-- The canonical natural isomorphism between the two tensor-coprojection pullback
    92	presheaves. -/
    93	noncomputable def tensorOverlapTheta :
    94	    (Over.map (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    95	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
    96	      (Over.map (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
    97	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
    98	  tensorOverlapCommon (C := C) (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L)) ≪≫
    99	    eqToIso (congrArg
   100	      (fun g => (Over.map g).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)
   101	      (tensorOverlapInl_comp_base (k := k) (L := L))) ≪≫
   102	    (tensorOverlapCommon (C := C) (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).symm
   103	
   104	/-! ## Pullback representations and the canonical scheme isomorphism -/
   105	
   106	variable {J : Over (Spec (.of L))}
   107	
   108	/-- The representation pulled back along the first tensor coprojection. -/
   109	noncomputable def tensorOverlapRepInl
   110	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
   111	    ((Over.map (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   112	      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy
   113	        ((Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :=
   114	  Functor.RepresentableBy.ofLeftAdjoint
   115	    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))) rep
   116	
   117	/-- The representation pulled back along the second tensor coprojection. -/
   118	noncomputable def tensorOverlapRepInr
   119	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
   120	    ((Over.map (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   121	      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy
   122	        ((Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :=
   123	  Functor.RepresentableBy.ofLeftAdjoint
   124	    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))) rep
   125	
   126	/-- The canonical representing-scheme isomorphism on the double tensor overlap. -/
   127	noncomputable def tensorOverlapIso
   128	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J) :
   129	    (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J ≅
   130	      (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))).obj J :=
   131	  Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
   132	    (tensorOverlapRepInl rep) (tensorOverlapRepInr rep)
   133	    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C))
   134	
   135	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   136	-- The expanded Over pullback comparison crosses several categorical
   137	-- functors; its definitional check exceeds Lean's default heartbeat budget.
   138	/-- Universal-element characterization of the tensor-overlap comparison. -/
   139	theorem tensorOverlapIso_homEquiv
   140	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J)
   141	    {T : Over (Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)))}
   142	    (f : T ⟶ (Over.pullback (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))).obj J) :
   143	    (tensorOverlapRepInr rep).homEquiv
   144	        (f ≫ (tensorOverlapIso rep).hom) =
   145	      (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C)).hom.app (Opposite.op T)
   146	        ((tensorOverlapRepInl rep).homEquiv f) :=
   147	  Functor.RepresentableBy.homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
   148	    (tensorOverlapRepInl rep) (tensorOverlapRepInr rep)
   149	    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C)) f
   150	
   151	/-! ## The triple tensor faces -/
   152	
   153	/-- The `1,2` Amitsur face on the triple tensor product. -/
   154	noncomputable def tensorTripleFace12 :
   155	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] (L ⊗[k] L))) ⟶ Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) :=
   156	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Module.descentFace₁₂ k L).toRingHom)
   157	
   158	/-- The `1,3` Amitsur face on the triple tensor product. -/
   159	noncomputable def tensorTripleFace13 :
   160	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] (L ⊗[k] L))) ⟶ Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) :=
   161	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Module.descentFace₁₃ k L).toRingHom)
   162	
   163	/-- The `2,3` Amitsur face on the triple tensor product. -/
   164	noncomputable def tensorTripleFace23 :
   165	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] (L ⊗[k] L))) ⟶ Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) :=
   166	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Module.descentFace₂₃ k L).toRingHom)
   167	
   168	/-- Projection from the triple overlap to the first copy of `Spec L`. -/
   169	noncomputable def tensorTripleCoord1 :=
   170	  tensorTripleFace12 (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L)
   171	
   172	/-- Projection from the triple overlap to the second copy of `Spec L`. -/
   173	noncomputable def tensorTripleCoord2 :=
   174	  tensorTripleFace12 (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L)
   175	
   176	/-- Projection from the triple overlap to the third copy of `Spec L`. -/
   177	noncomputable def tensorTripleCoord3 :=
   178	  tensorTripleFace13 (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L)
   179	
   180	/-- The second coordinate is also the left coordinate of the `2,3` face. -/
   181	lemma tensorTripleCoord2_eq_face23_inl :
   182	    tensorTripleCoord2 (k := k) (L := L) =
   183	      tensorTripleFace23 (k := k) (L := L) ≫
   184	        tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L) := by
   185	  simp only [tensorTripleCoord2, tensorTripleFace12, tensorTripleFace23,
   186	    tensorOverlapInl, tensorOverlapInr]
   187	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
   188	  congr 1
   189	
   190	/-- The left coordinate of the `1,3` face is the first triple coordinate. -/
   191	lemma tensorTripleFace13_inl :
   192	    tensorTripleFace13 (k := k) (L := L) ≫
   193	        tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L) =
   194	      tensorTripleCoord1 (k := k) (L := L) := by
   195	  simp only [tensorTripleCoord1, tensorTripleFace12, tensorTripleFace13,
   196	    tensorOverlapInl]
   197	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
   198	  congr 1
   199	
   200	/-- The right coordinate of the `1,3` face is the third triple coordinate. -/
   201	lemma tensorTripleFace13_inr :
   202	    tensorTripleFace13 (k := k) (L := L) ≫
   203	        tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L) =
   204	      tensorTripleCoord3 (k := k) (L := L) := by
   205	  rfl
   206	
   207	/-- The third coordinate is also the right coordinate of the `2,3` face. -/
   208	lemma tensorTripleCoord3_eq_face23_inr :
   209	    tensorTripleCoord3 (k := k) (L := L) =
   210	      tensorTripleFace23 (k := k) (L := L) ≫
   211	        tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L) := by
   212	  simp only [tensorTripleCoord3, tensorTripleFace13, tensorTripleFace23,
   213	    tensorOverlapInr]
   214	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
   215	  congr 1
   216	
   217	/-- The common map from the triple overlap to `Spec k`. -/
   218	noncomputable def tensorTripleBase :=
   219	  tensorTripleCoord1 (k := k) (L := L) ≫ tensorOverlapBase (k := k) (L := L)
   220	
   300	    (tensorTripleCoord3_comp_base (k := k) (L := L))
   301	
   302	/-! The following three comparisons are the literal pullbacks of the double-overlap
   303	theta.  The explicit equality arguments retain the proof-bearing scheme-map casts for
   304	the `2,3` and `1,3` faces. -/
   305	
   306	noncomputable def tensorTripleTheta12_face :
   307	    (Over.map (tensorTripleCoord1 (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   308	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
   309	      (Over.map (tensorTripleCoord2 (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   310	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   311	  Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafFace
   312	    (tensorTripleCoord1 (k := k) (L := L))
   313	    (tensorTripleCoord2 (k := k) (L := L))
   314	    (tensorTripleFace12 (k := k) (L := L))
   315	    (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))
   316	    (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))
   317	    rfl rfl (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C))
   318	
   319	noncomputable def tensorTripleTheta23_face :
   320	    (Over.map (tensorTripleCoord2 (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   321	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
   322	      (Over.map (tensorTripleCoord3 (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   323	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   324	  Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafFace
   325	    (tensorTripleCoord2 (k := k) (L := L))
   326	    (tensorTripleCoord3 (k := k) (L := L))
   327	    (tensorTripleFace23 (k := k) (L := L))
   328	    (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))
   329	    (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))
   330	    (tensorTripleCoord2_eq_face23_inl (k := k) (L := L))
   331	    (tensorTripleCoord3_eq_face23_inr (k := k) (L := L))
   332	    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C))
   333	
   334	noncomputable def tensorTripleTheta13_face :
   335	    (Over.map (tensorTripleCoord1 (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   336	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
   337	      (Over.map (tensorTripleCoord3 (k := k) (L := L))).op ⋙
   338	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   339	  Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafFace
   340	    (tensorTripleCoord1 (k := k) (L := L))
   341	    (tensorTripleCoord3 (k := k) (L := L))
   342	    (tensorTripleFace13 (k := k) (L := L))
   343	    (tensorOverlapInl (k := k) (L := L))
   344	    (tensorOverlapInr (k := k) (L := L))
   345	    (tensorTripleFace13_inl (k := k) (L := L)).symm
   346	    (tensorTripleFace13_inr (k := k) (L := L)).symm
   347	    (tensorOverlapTheta (C := C))
   348	
   349	-- Expanding the proof-bearing Over-map reassociations and theta common-base
   350	-- comparisons exceeds Lean's default heartbeat budget on these three faces.
   351	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   352	lemma tensorTripleTheta12_face_eq :
   353	    tensorTripleTheta12_face (k := k) (L := L) (C := C) =
   354	      tensorTripleTheta12 (k := k) (L := L) (C := C) := by
   355	  unfold tensorTripleTheta12_face tensorTripleTheta12 tensorTripleTheta
   356	  simp only [Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafFace,
   357	    tensorTripleCommon, pic0BaseCommon]
   358	  simp only [tensorTripleCoord1, tensorTripleCoord2]
   359	  rw [Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafOfEq_eq_canonical]
   360	  rw [Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafCommon_comp]
   361	  rw [Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafOfEq_eq_canonical]
   362	  rw [Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.mapCompPresheafCommon_comp]

   370	    Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, NatTrans.comp_app,
   371	    Functor.isoWhiskerLeft_hom, Functor.whiskerLeft_app,

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds.
